capabilities: Render a force-directed graph that stays smooth on vaults with tens of thousands of notes
Save and restore the graph layout between sessions
Filter the graph by search, tags, orphans, attachments and excluded folders, with colour groups and hover cards
Show a local graph of a note and its neighbours
Arrange notes into shape layouts (honeycomb, spiral galaxy, solar system and others) and add optional 3D and motion effects
extras: Benchmarks come from one MacBook on synthetic vaults with random links, one run each, and the author lists caveats in docs/comparison.md. Not tested on mobile; tested on macOS only. Formerly named Fast Graph (releases 0.1.0–0.2.0); old settings do not carry over. Needs Obsidian 1.13.4 or newer.
intentEvidence: How fast is it, compared with Obsidian's built-in graph?
problem: Obsidian's built-in graph view becomes slow, janky and memory-hungry on vaults with tens of thousands of notes.

relations.evidence: The layout follows the d3-force model, written from its public description (no d3 code is included).

summary: Graph view plugin that renders very large vaults smoothly, with saved layouts, filters, a local graph, shape layouts and optional 3D.
